1. Executive Summary & Objective Verification

Component 3 of research project J26-IT339 establishes an Explainable, Supervised Machine Learning regression pipeline capable of predicting personalized tourist enjoyment for destinations across Sri Lanka. The primary research target specified in the proposal requires a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) ≤ 0.70 on a 1.0 to 5.0 star enjoyment rating scale.

The model was trained directly on the complete validated dataset of 16,156 raw TripAdvisor reviews expanded into 48,516 archetype-stratified instances (solo, couple, family).

2. Dataset Profile & Feature Engineering

  • Master Dataset File: C:\Users\User\Downloads\Tourism_Master_Validated (1).csv
  • Total Raw Verified Reviews: 16,156 visitor reviews across 76 major tourism destinations in Sri Lanka.
  • Total Stratified Samples: 48,516 instances across 3 distinct personas:
    • Solo Travelers: 16,172 samples
    • Couple Travelers: 16,172 samples
    • Family Travelers: 16,172 samples
  • Training Split (80%): 38,812 records | Unseen Test Split (20%): 9,704 records

3. Model Architecture & 5-Fold Cross Validation

The machine learning pipeline combines an automated ColumnTransformer with an ensemble RandomForestRegressor:

  • Categorical Preprocessor: OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown='ignore') for category, traveler_type, and origin_country.
  • Numerical Preprocessor: passthrough for vader_sentiment, foreigner_fee_usd, and typical_dwell_minutes.
  • Ensemble Configuration: 120 decision trees, max tree depth of 16, min samples split = 4, min samples leaf = 2, random seed = 42, all CPU cores (n_jobs=-1).
